London, 12<sup>th</sup> March 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**Ford Motor Co** ., the first U.S. automaker to reach a mid-contract union agreement, said labour concessions will save about $375 million this year and allow consolidation of vehicle assembly between two Michigan factories.  The automaker said contract changes ratified by the United Auto Workers union on March 9 permit the use of stock to pay as much as $6.5 billion to a Voluntary Employee Beneficiary Association retiree health-care fund. Ford will halt assembly of the Ford Focus small car at a Wayne, Michigan, factory and shift production to an adjacent plant, said Joe Hinrichs, Ford’s manufacturing chief. Ford will save $250 million of the $500 million from ending the cost-of-living adjustments and bonuses for employees. It will only realize about 75 % of the $500 million in annual savings this year, Hinrichs said. The new agreement will trim hourly labor and benefit costs to $55 an hour from $60. Ford’s labor costs may fall to $50 an hour by 2011, if the car market improves. That would bring Ford close to parity with the U.S. plants of Asian and European automakers, which have labor costs of about $48 or $49 an hour. The UAW deal helps Ford avoid government aid as collapsing car sales pressure operating cash. Ford’s U.S. sales fell 48 % in February from a year earlier.  The union concessions include elimination of annual bonuses and cost-of-living pay increases. Ford, which consumed $21.2 billion in cash last year, has not borrowed money from a U.S. Treasury program that has loaned $17.4 billion so far to GM and Chrysler. _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**Shares in French carmakers Renault and PSA Peugeot Citroen** rose sharply on Wednesday on market talk of a merger between the groups, traders said, as Renault denied the rumor.  A spokesman for PSA Peugeot Citroen declined to comment, while an analyst said a deal between the two was unlikely. At 1110 GMT (7:10 a.m. EDT) Peugeot shares were up 7.9 % at 14.95 euros and Renault shares were up 7.67 % at 13.05 euros, while the CAC Paris market index was up 1.02 % and the DJ Stoxx European autos sector index was up 2.78%. PSA’s announcement that it had appointed Barnaby Noble -- a former vice president of mergers and acquisitions at Alstom -- as director of strategy and business development fueled speculation, according to Credit Suisse analyst Stuart Pearson.  Pearson added that he thought a tie-up between the two groups was extremely unlikely and would not be allowed by the French state, a Renault shareholder.  Industry watchers have predicted that the sector -- hit by falling sales amid a global economic slump -- will see increased consolidation as companies fight for survival. _Source:  Reuters_ 

**Toyota Motor Corp.’s** U.S. sales chief said production cuts are bringing vehicle inventory in the market to a normal level even as sales still drop.  Toyota, second in U.S. sales to General Motors Corp., expects to have a 45-day s

upply by April or May compared with a record 100-day supply of cars and trucks at the end of 2008, Jim Lentz, president of Toyota Motor Sales USA, said yesterday.  The worst U.S. auto market in 28 years led Toyota, which passed GM in global sales last year, to cut output at all auto and engine factories in the U.S., Canada and Mexico, and create its first buyout offer for workers. Failures among suppliers may disrupt production even as inventories fall.  “The biggest challenge that we face is really on the supplier side of the business,” Lentz said. _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**Panasonic** have launched a rubbish-processing machine. The main unit is the RISAIKURA MS-N53. The recycler can take up to 2 kg of organic garbage, such as food scraps. It mixes them together and uses a combination of a platinum- palladium catalyst and heat to break it down. The end result is compost.  The unit operates off mains electricity and consumes about 800 W of power. It measures 268Ч365Ч550 mm, and weighs about 12 kg. A smaller model, the MS-N23, has a capacity of 1 kg and is just over half the size. The MS-N53 will sell for ¥85,000 when it comes on the market on April 25, and the MSN-23 will cost ¥65,000. 

_Source: The Japan Times_
